name: Wolfkin
body:
Wolfkin are tall, athletic, wolf-headed humanoids who are often mistaken for werewolves or rougarous. Also known among some as ?dogfolk,? they are reclusive and found almost exclusively in the world’s most remote regions.

Appearance

Wolfkin are furry bestial humanoids with heads that greatly resemble wolves, coyotes, or other canines. Their wolflike muzzles are filled with sharp teeth that can deliver powerful bites, as well as giving them a fierce appearance. This causes them to often be confused with werewolves, a misunderstanding that causes wolfkin great dismay.

Wolfkin typically have gray, brown, or reddish fur, but snow white, coal black, and mottled patterns have also been noted. As a hunting and gathering culture, they prefer simple clothing and armor, usually hides and leathers dyed in tribal colors and patterns.

Social

Most wolfkin subsist in traditional huntergatherer cultures, usually following large herd animals across desolate windswept plains or arctic tundra. Because of their association with werewolves, and the prejudice they have experienced as a result, wolfkin are wary of trading with others.

Their largest settlements tend to remain hidden in remote hills and forests, their location known only to a few.

Meanwhile, wandering wolfkin deal firmly with those they encounter. Whie they rarely resort to violence unprovoked, they are not afraid to negotiate aggressively and defense their lands, for hundreds of miles in every direction, from unwanted incursion-at least without paying the proper tribute.

Among themselves, wolfkin organize in tightly-knit packs. They are extremely loyal to their allies. There is no difference between the concepts of family and friend in the mind of a wolfkin-while their trust can be difficult to obtain, once you are accepted into the pack, you are considered family, regardless of your ancestry or origin.

If there is an exception to this rule, it is in the wolfkin’s undying hatred for lycanthropes and shapechangers of all kinds, as well as their deep disgust for gnolls. While many have also had poor dealings with other groups, including goblinoids, humans, and orcs, even these are not completely irredeemable-but it is almost unheard of for a gnoll or werewolf to be accepted by an individual wolfkin, let alone a pack.

Alignment and Religion

Many wolfkin are Neutral, feeling the necessity of pragmatism imposed by the ruthlessness of survival in the harshest of environments. However, many also feel the strong lure of idealism that informs their decisions, pulling them toward a more moral-driven motivation. For most, this call leans more toward Lawful than Chaotic, and more toward Good than Evil, although there are exceptions to this rule.

Wolfkin have their own pantheon of deities, although their names differ from pack to pack. Many are closely related to a core concept, such as “rain” or “the hunt,” and so wolfkin of different packs will discuss their gods as “The God of Rain” and “The God of the Hunt” rather than using the proper names they use among themselves, so as not to cause confusion. While their ceremonies and practices vary as much as the names used for them, the spells and clerical powers they offer seem to be consistent, leading to a more-or-less unified clergy across the far-flung wolfkin culture.

Names

Some typical wolfkin names include the following (choose or roll 1d12): 1 Bledig, 2 Daciana, 3 Dolfus, 4 Grenard, 5 Lobo, 6 Louvell, 7 Lupita, 8 Orfilia, 9 Otsana, 10 Ralf, 11 Ulfa, 12 Vilko

Common Traits
Ability Score Modifiers You are strong and perceptive, but your ways are simple. Your ability score modifiers are +2 Str, +2 Wis, -2 Int [standard]. (0)
Size As a Medium creature, you have no bonuses or penalties due to size. (0)
Type You are a Humanoid with the wolfkin subtype. (0)
Speed Your base speed is 30 feet. (0)
Languages You begin play speaking Common and Wolfkin. If you have a high Intelligence score, you can choose from any of the following languages: Elven, Gnoll, Goblin, Rougarou, Shoony, and Sylvan. (0)
Other Traits
Bite You have a bite attack. This is a primary natural weapon that deals 1d4 damage. (2)
Expert Rider In their pursuit of great herds of animals across the plains, many wolfkin are born to the saddle. You gain a +2 species bonus on all Ride checks. (2)
Hatred You gain a +1 species bonus on attack rolls against humanoid creatures of the gnoll and shapechanger subtypes. (1)
Low-light vision You can see twice as far as a human in starlight, moonlight, torchlight, and similar conditions of poor illumination. You retain the ability to distinguish color and detail under these conditions. (1)
Scent You have the scent universal monster ability. (4)
Total: 10 RP (standard)
Variants
Guardian

Sturdy and hard-working, these stoic wolfkin often bear a resemblance to large dog breeds like huskies or bulldogs. You gain +2 Con, +2 Wis, -2 Cha. This alters your ability score modifiers.

Hunter

Hunter wolfkin are smaller and slenderer than most of their kin, but are known for making excellent trackers. You gain +2 Dex, +2 Wis, -2 Con. This alters your ability score modifiers.

Alternate Traits
Emissary You are skilled at making friends and maintaining alliances. You gain a +2 species bonus on Diplomacy checks. This trait replaces expert rider.
Ferocious You know how to make the most of your predatory appearance. You gain a +2 species bonus on Intimidate checks. This trait replaces expert rider.
Keen Ears You gain a +2 species bonus on all sound-based Perception checks. This trait replaces low-light vision.
Natural Armor Your thick, wrinkly skin provides an extra layer of protection. You gain a +1 natural armor bonus to AC. This trait replaces bite.
Padded Feet You gain a +2 species bonus to all Acrobatics and Stealth checks provided you are barefoot or wearing soft covering on your feet, such as leather boots. This trait replaces scent.
Specialized You have devoted yourself to a particular talent. You receive a +2 species bonus on any one Craft, Perform, or Profession skill of your choice. This trait replaces expert rider.
Vigilant You are always on the lookout for danger. You gain Alertness as a bonus feat. This trait replaces hatred and low-light vision.
Weapon Familiarity You are proficient with the greatclub, longbow, shortbow, and spear. You treat the broadspear CW and horse bow MM as martial weapons instead of exotic ones. This trait replaces bite.
Favored Class Bonuses
Barbarian Add +1/2 on critical hit confirmation rolls for attacks made with unarmed strikes or natural weapons (maximum bonus of +4). This bonus does not stack with Critical Focus.
Cavalier Add a +1/2 bonus on Ride checks and a +1/2 bonus on Diplomacy checks to gather information.
Cleric Add +1/3 to the amount of damage dealt or damage healed when you use channel energy.
Druid Add a +1/2 bonus on Intimidate checks.
Fighter Choose the drag or trip combat maneuver. Add +1/3 to your CMB when attempting this maneuver (maximum bonus of +4).
Monk Add a +1/4 bonus on combat maneuver checks made to grapple or trip.
Ranger Choose a weapon from the following list: bite, broadspear CW, greatclub, horse bow MM, longbow, shortbow, or spear. Add +1/2 on critical hit confirmation rolls made while using that weapon (maximum bonus of +4). This bonus does not stack with Critical Focus.
Rogue Add a +1/2 bonus on Acrobatics checks to jump and Intimidate checks to demoralize.

Awesome Ancestries: Fantasy Animal Humanoids, Vol. 3 - Born to Be Wild. © 2025, Far Distant Future Publishing; Author: Bryan Mangum.
